previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A young woman with a history of tracheobronchomalacia, bronchopulmonary dysplasia, and tracheostomy dependence was admitted for cough with bloody, mucopurulent tracheostomy secretions and post-viral symptoms. She had recently been treated for presumed viral bronchitis but continued to have dyspnea and malaise. A bronchoscopy revealed granulation tissue without active bleeding, and doxycycline was started to cover for possible bacterial infection. Her respiratory status improved, and she was weaned from supplemental oxygen to room air. She was discharged home with a seven-day course of oral doxycycline and follow-up arranged with her PCP and interventional pulmonology.

PATIENT SUMMARY:
====================
Ms. ___ is a ___ w/ PMH bronchopulmonary dysplasia c/b 
larygneal stenosis & tracheostomy dependence(Portex #8) who 
presents for cough and dyspnea. Also with increased secretion 
production from her trach associated with neck pain. Admitted 
for concern for trachiobronchitis in the setting of recurrent 
granulation tissue at the site of her trach. 

====================
ACUTE ISSUES:
====================
#Trachiobronchitis: The patient has a history of recurrent 
trachiobronchitis with history of colonization with pseudomonas 
(sensitive to cipro in ___, MRSA, and staph epidermis. She 
presented with one week of increased secretions, pain, dyspnea, 
cough. CXR and EKG were reassuring. There was a low suspicion 
for PE due to other probable cause of symptoms and no known risk 
factors for PE (no immobility, travel). Sputum cultures were 
contaminated. IP was consulted and recommended starting broad 
spectrum antibiotics - vancomycin and ciprofloxacin: D1 ___. 
On ___, the patient underwent a flex bronch with excision of 
granulation tissue performed by IP. Findings included: moderate 
amount of thick clear/yellow secretions which were sent for 
culture and a significant stenosis at the site of her trach and 
supraglottic area. ENT was consulted and recommended an 
outpatient work up. ENT follow up was arranged. Gram stain from 
bronchoscopy showed gram positive cocci in pairs. The patient 
has previously grown strep B. Antibiotics were changed to 
ciprofloxacin alone per IP recs to complete a 7-day course of 
possible trachiobronchitis. Cultures from bronchoscopy are 
pending at the time of discharge.
